distinct_myths.stat: Fresha shows six of 22 services above the fold before 'See all'
distinct_myths.why_fake: Cited as the strongest proof point for the fold-item band, but a fresh fetch of the same live page found only 4 shown, not 6. Downgraded to a range, not a clean match.

distinct_myths.stat: Users form a first impression of a webpage in 50ms, sourced to Tuch et al. 2012
distinct_myths.why_fake: The well-established source for the 50ms figure is Lindgaard et al. 2006, not Tuch 2012. Tuch's paper is real but narrower, and its exact exposure duration could not even be confirmed.

distinct_myths.stat: Treatwell's homepage is about 60% text / 40% visual
distinct_myths.why_fake: An independent re-look at the same page estimated the opposite ratio, 80-85% text / 15-20% visual. Both numbers are ungrounded eyeball guesses, not pixel measurements.

distinct_myths.stat: Booksy's profile structure has an exact 7-item block including a discrete 'staff photos' item
distinct_myths.why_fake: Booksy's real documented structure only has a general 'portfolio/showcase' item, not a discrete staff-photos block. The exact match was false precision.

distinct_myths.stat: Uber's internal design critique flagged imagery as present but not prioritized
distinct_myths.why_fake: Sourced only to a third-party teardown blog, not any real Uber document. An unverifiable narrative dressed as an internal fact.

distinct_myths.stat: Uber's 2023 app redesign uses a 'bento grid' layout
distinct_myths.why_fake: Real press coverage only describes a simplified two-option homescreen; none of it uses the words 'grid' or 'bento'. A screenshot interpretation was layered onto unrelated press text.

distinct_myths.stat: 67% of top-100 ProductHunt SaaS products use a bento layout
distinct_myths.why_fake: Untraceable, unsourced statistic; correctly caught and kept out of the shipped text.

distinct_myths.stat: Bento layouts drive 15-25% higher mid-page engagement
distinct_myths.why_fake: Untraceable, unsourced statistic; correctly caught and kept out of the shipped text.

distinct_myths.stat: A DEV Community six-month retrospective names calm design / anti-maximalism as the trend that stuck
distinct_myths.why_fake: The real article says the opposite: bento grids and dark mode held up, kinetic typography and glassmorphism faded. It never mentions calm design.

distinct_myths.stat: Showit and Figma's Resource Library document a 96-128px section-gap shift
distinct_myths.why_fake: Invented number; the actual Showit article only gives a vague '20% more whitespace' tip with no pixel figures anywhere.

distinct_myths.stat: 1140-1280px max content width, per the Showit roundup
distinct_myths.why_fake: The Showit article never mentions a max-width figure at all. The number is a real industry convention (Bootstrap-style containers) misattributed to a source that doesn't say it.

distinct_myths.stat: involve.me names fewer/larger sections with bigger gaps as an explicit named 2026 trend
distinct_myths.why_fake: The article treats whitespace only as generic best practice with no named trend and no pixel numbers.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell heroes run 25-30% of the first viewport
distinct_myths.why_fake: A live re-check measured Fresha at 40-50% and Treatwell at 30-40%, both above the claimed band. Neither pass used real pixel measurement.

distinct_myths.stat: Doctolib's hero takes 5-10% of page height
distinct_myths.why_fake: Unconfirmed; a fetch of doctolib.fr only returned footer/nav markup, so the actual hero was never seen by whoever cited this number.

distinct_myths.stat: Every search/filter zero-results CTA in the field is a solid brand-color fill
distinct_myths.why_fake: Refuted by re-scouting: Skyscanner uses a neutral-outline pill, GitHub uses a plain text link, Walmart ships no CTA at all. The field is mixed, not a wall.

distinct_myths.stat: CRED's empty-trips illustration is a single-ink-outline / monochrome style
distinct_myths.why_fake: The real illustration has color fill (tan/beige shape with red/pink accents), not a strict monochrome outline.

distinct_myths.stat: Solen's EmptyStateDiscovery banner is 200px tall (about 25% of an 812px viewport)
distinct_myths.why_fake: The live component code actually renders 220px (about 27%); the cited number came from a stale doc, not the live code.

distinct_myths.stat: Container queries have about 94% browser support as of December 2025
distinct_myths.why_fake: Chronologically impossible: caniuse's current mid-2026 figure is only 92.6%, and support only grows over time, so a December-2025 number should be lower, not higher.

distinct_myths.stat: Solen's responsive grid ladder flatly mismatches the Fresha/Airbnb reference
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstated: the locked rule already has a map-open exception that matches what was observed; the only untested gap is the map-closed state.

distinct_myths.stat: Solen's DateTimePicker component proves out per-breakpoint responsive collapse
distinct_myths.why_fake: Its real behavior is a per-product-context choice (search always calendar, booking always strip), not a viewport-breakpoint collapse. Citing it conflates two different mechanisms.

distinct_myths.stat: Airbnb's grid collapses in six steps: 6-5-4-3-2-1 columns as viewport narrows
distinct_myths.why_fake: Directly contradicted by this same research's own live-render check: a flat 2-column hold to 768px then a straight drop to 1 column at 375px, no gradual descent.

distinct_myths.stat: The search-results grid is Solen's highest-traffic imagery-bearing surface
distinct_myths.why_fake: Implies real analytics data that doesn't exist. Solen is pre-launch with no live customers, so no traffic ranking among surfaces is measurable.

distinct_myths.stat: Foundey's 'Stepper UI Best Practices' article is a credentialed source for a 300ms transition rule
distinct_myths.why_fake: It's an uncredentialed startup marketing blog with no cited study behind its number, published the day before this research ran.

distinct_myths.stat: About 70.22% of e-commerce carts are abandoned (digidrub.com)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Unsourced blog statistic; correctly caught as a myth and excluded from the shipped text.

distinct_myths.stat: Uber's Base design system blocks a new token merge in CI until it passes WCAG and brand checks
distinct_myths.why_fake: Unverifiable; neither Uber's own Base launch blog post nor the baseweb GitHub README mentions any such CI/lint gate.

distinct_myths.stat: The W3C DTCG token-format spec (Oct 2025) is a stable standard
distinct_myths.why_fake: False framing; the live spec page explicitly labels itself a preview Draft Community Group Report carrying a 'do not implement' warning.

distinct_myths.stat: Atlassian documents its token grammar as 'Foundation.Property.Variant.State'
distinct_myths.why_fake: This exact naming convention could not be confirmed as an official Atlassian term; it reads as a paraphrase presented as a quoted label.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha's search-results cards are thin: photo, name, rating, address, category, no price (about 5 fields)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Factually inverted: live Fresha search cards actually show name, distance, category, and up to three priced/timed services plus a service-count link. The thin card described is Fresha's homepage carousel, not its search results.

distinct_myths.stat: Booksy cards run about 8-10 fields versus Fresha's about 5 fields (a density contrast)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Backwards, a direct consequence of the Fresha-card inversion above; Fresha's real search card is at least as field-dense as Booksy's.

distinct_myths.stat: Pinterest shows about 3.3 rows (6-7 tiles) per 812px fold
distinct_myths.why_fake: False precision; Mobbin captures only support a rough 'about 3 rows' qualitatively, not a decimal-accurate measurement.

distinct_myths.stat: A 5-student study validated the Lok/Feiner/Ngai visual-balance algorithm
distinct_myths.why_fake: Fabricated; the actual paper's own PDF reports zero human subjects, only a computational benchmark demo.

distinct_myths.stat: Solen's proposed balance formula (weighted centroid vs geometric center) matches the Lok/Feiner/Ngai model
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstated; the real paper computes crystallographic balance from a per-pixel weight map, not a centroid-offset number. It's loose inspiration, not a derivation.

distinct_myths.stat: The Jahanian visual-balance paper comes from MIT CSAIL
distinct_myths.why_fake: False institutional tag; the paper is Purdue-era research, years before Jahanian's later MIT CSAIL affiliation.

distinct_myths.stat: American Airlines' checkout screen shows an $87.40 total that violates the ink-price lock (a specific Mobbin screen ID)
distinct_myths.why_fake: That Mobbin screen ID cannot be found anywhere in the catalog after three separate targeted searches; reads as a hallucinated citation and was cut entirely.

distinct_myths.stat: HotelTonight's sign-up screen uses a dark purple theme (a specific Mobbin screen ID)
distinct_myths.why_fake: This screen also cannot be located in Mobbin's catalog under any search phrasing; cut entirely as fabricated.

distinct_myths.stat: Airbnb's design docs quote Rausch red as reserved for 'one or two moments' only
distinct_myths.why_fake: The cited source never contains this quote; its real text is a more general 'don't make Rausch a default fill' statement with no numeric quantification.

distinct_myths.stat: Peerspace's booking commit CTA is solid black
distinct_myths.why_fake: Wrong; live screenshots show the actual CTA ('Request to Book') is solid purple/violet, not black.

distinct_myths.stat: Galen Framework defaults to a ~12px max alignment mismatch with a 30px scan region
distinct_myths.why_fake: Refuted; Galen has no such published default, and the '30px' figure is actually an unrelated image-diff color-tolerance parameter, not a spatial alignment threshold.

distinct_myths.stat: Uber runs a 'Base Counter' tool with daily CI auto-ticketing and a named 'Feature Review Readiness' step
distinct_myths.why_fake: Could not be found via any search or direct URL check on Uber's blog; the invented specificity is a classic hallucination pattern.

distinct_myths.stat: A Chromatic/Percy visual-regression check means a PR literally cannot merge while unresolved
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstated; this only happens if a team explicitly configures it as a required branch-protection check, it isn't automatic.

distinct_myths.stat: Eleken's design-QA checklist has exactly 17 steps
distinct_myths.why_fake: The specific page 404'd; the precise step count is unconfirmed and was dropped, keeping only the general claim that such a checklist exists in this genre.

distinct_myths.stat: Figma shipped an AI design-review assistant at Config 2026
distinct_myths.why_fake: Zero corroboration found across two searches and a direct fetch of figma.com/config; stays an unconfirmed claim.

distinct_myths.stat: Stitch Fix's Style Shuffle has generated over 1 billion ratings
distinct_myths.why_fake: Off by 10x; Stitch Fix's own newsroom and LinkedIn material state over 10 billion interactions/ratings.

distinct_myths.stat: 80%+ of Stitch Fix's 4 million+ customers use Style Shuffle
distinct_myths.why_fake: Untraceable to any Stitch Fix publication across two search engines; cut entirely as an invented precision figure attached to a real program.

distinct_myths.stat: A ScienceDirect paper describes LLM-assisted hybrid interfaces for remote repertory-grid interviews ('Q-Survey')
distinct_myths.why_fake: Could not be located under any phrasing across two search engines; very likely a hallucinated citation, downgraded to myth and removed.

distinct_myths.stat: Fransella/Bell/Bannister's manual specifies stopping repertory-grid elicitation after 2 consecutive triads with zero new poles, typically 6-10 triads for an 8-10 element pool
distinct_myths.why_fake: The manual's real guidance is only 'run to saturation, not a fixed count'; the specific numbers aren't in the source.

distinct_myths.stat: Cornsweet's staircase method specifies stopping after 3 reversals, averaging the last 3
distinct_myths.why_fake: Cornsweet 1962 only says to continue 'until many reversals are obtained'; it never specifies 3, and classic practice often runs 6-8 reversals.

distinct_myths.stat: NN/g names 'Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options' as an official article/doctrine
distinct_myths.why_fake: This exact title could not be found on NN/g's own article index or via any search; downgraded to an independently-observed convention, not verified NN/g doctrine.

distinct_myths.stat: 40.4% average design-token coverage across 375 audited production sites, per zeroheight
distinct_myths.why_fake: This figure does not appear anywhere in the actual zeroheight report (a 147-practitioner stability survey with no site-coverage metric); a genuine conflation of two unrelated studies.

distinct_myths.stat: A 'Design Systems Collective' study found only 7.5% of 375 sites got token coverage right
distinct_myths.why_fake: Misattributed; that domain doesn't resolve. The real publisher is OverlayQA, whose actual stat is '90%+ coverage puts you in the top 7.5%', a different framing.

distinct_myths.stat: OverlayQA's design-token drift taxonomy names three subtypes
distinct_myths.why_fake: Incomplete; the real taxonomy names five subtypes, and two were omitted without being flagged as existing.

distinct_myths.stat: NN/g's Proximity article gives an illustrative spacing ladder: 4px / 8px / 16px / 32px / 64px
distinct_myths.why_fake: False; the real article is purely qualitative about Gestalt proximity and contains zero pixel values. The ladder was invented and dressed up as an NN/g claim.

distinct_myths.stat: The 1.25 minimum spacing-ratio floor is borrowed from EightShapes and Utopia.fyi's spacing-scale essays
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstated; EightShapes' worked example uses a ~2x doubling progression, and Utopia.fyi's ratio presets are documented for type scale, not spacing. Neither endorses 1.25 for whitespace.

distinct_myths.stat: GitHub Projects' Priority field is a platform-convention anchor for a fixed severity scale
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overclaimed; GitHub's own docs confirm Priority is a user-created custom field with no canonical option set.

distinct_myths.stat: Miro is a 3-tier convention anchor for the low end of the severity tier-count band
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overclaimed; Miro has no native priority or severity feature at all. The captured example was one board's freeform design choice.

distinct_myths.stat: Airtable's group headers literally read 'PRIORITY [tier] + Count N'
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overclaims precision; this is more plausibly a paraphrase of the UI than a verbatim quoted string.

distinct_myths.stat: Airbnb's Help Center shows a 6-level breadcrumb path
distinct_myths.why_fake: Not a verified capture; a spot-check found only 5-level breadcrumbs on other topics, and this exact path returned no matching screen. Reads as an invented illustrative example.

distinct_myths.stat: UXPin documents a 'three-tap rule' for interaction design
distinct_myths.why_fake: The most likely source URL 404s; the attribution is unconfirmed, though the broader point (a folklore tap-count rule with no data behind it) is plausible on its own.

distinct_myths.stat: 70% of users are link-first / 30% are search-first, per Katz and Byrne 2003 (as cited by NN/g)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Fabricated; the real paper found a wide, mixed distribution of browsing and searching behavior, not a fixed 70/30 split, and no NN/g page could be found citing this number.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha's homepage renders 13 category pills with zero signup wall
distinct_myths.why_fake: The number doesn't hold up; a live re-navigation shows only a search bar and header, zero category pills anywhere. The no-signup-wall finding is real, the 13-pills figure isn't.

distinct_myths.stat: Never put a corner Skip link on a screen that also has a bar-progress indicator
distinct_myths.why_fake: Contradicted by the draft's own cited evidence: Tinder's interest-picker screen has a progress bar, a corner Skip link, and a counted Next button all at once.

distinct_myths.stat: 82% of users prefer dark mode for AI apps, and voice-interface usage grew 65% year over year (Groovy Web)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Unsourced agency-blog percentages; correctly pre-screened and excluded as myths.

distinct_myths.stat: Doctolib's footer shows six trust/credibility marks
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstated; live reverification found seven to eight distinct marks, not six.

distinct_myths.stat: Viator, Duolingo, Klima, Notion, Peerspace, and CAVA all use red for destructive-action buttons
distinct_myths.why_fake: Five of these six apps have zero backing evidence entries anywhere in the research; only Notion's red delete buttons were actually confirmed live.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha is broadly ink-monochrome on destructive commit actions
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overgeneralized; Fresha's own admin panel shows red 'Delete' buttons on training and shift-deletion modals. The ink-only pattern is confirmed only on the client-facing cancel modal.

distinct_myths.stat: Kiwi.com, Tripadvisor, and Plausible Analytics all name the specific failure reason on a promo-code error
distinct_myths.why_fake: Plausible's actual message ('You need to enter a valid discount code') is generic and doesn't name a specific cause; only two of the three actually clear that bar.

distinct_myths.stat: Airbnb's iOS Accessibility screen has toggles for 'Wheelchair accessible vehicle,' 'Descriptive audio,' and 'Minimize walking time,' each with a full explanatory sentence
distinct_myths.why_fake: Misattributed; that exact screen and copy belongs to Waymo, not Airbnb. Airbnb's real screen has only short one-line captions.

distinct_myths.stat: Mejtoft, Langstrom, and Soderstrom (2018) prove skeleton screens beat spinners on perceived speed
distinct_myths.why_fake: Misrepresents the paper; its own abstract states it found no significant differences between the pages tested.

distinct_myths.stat: Harrison et al.'s 'Rethinking the Progress Bar' found backward-rippling progress feels 10-11% faster (p<0.001)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Invented precision; this magnitude and p-value could not be verified from any accessible source and isn't in the existing, more conservative internal citation.

distinct_myths.stat: NN/g says NBC's loading pattern 'reads as a glitch, not a loading cue'
distinct_myths.why_fake: Misquoted; the actual NN/g article says it's 'essentially equivalent to a spinner' and warns users will assume the page isn't working and abandon it.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha's booking flow keeps a 'Continue' button visible but greyed out before a service is selected
distinct_myths.why_fake: The closest matching real screen actually uses a button labeled 'Add to booking', not 'Continue'.

distinct_myths.stat: Alice Chen, UX Content Collective blog (2026)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Very likely a fabricated source; the domain uxcontentcollective.com does not exist (DNS failure).

distinct_myths.stat: NN/g's guidance converges on a 7th-8th grade reading level for error copy
distinct_myths.why_fake: Citation-mixing error: attached to the wrong NN/g articles (which don't mention reading level at all); the real NN/g figure, from a different article, is 6-8th grade.

distinct_myths.stat: PlainLanguage.gov/digital.gov states copy should be written at an 8th-grade reading level or below
distinct_myths.why_fake: The current live guide page doesn't state any explicit grade-level number; downgraded pending a citable source.

distinct_myths.stat: GOV.UK writes copy for a 9-year-old's reading age
distinct_myths.why_fake: Could not be confirmed on any current live GOV.UK or GDS page, despite being a commonly repeated factoid.

distinct_myths.stat: NN/g says a half-built/half-shipped dark theme is worse than no dark theme at all
distinct_myths.why_fake: Fabricated; the real article's conclusion is the opposite, recommending a user-facing dark-mode toggle rather than an all-or-nothing framing.

distinct_myths.stat: NN/g found dark mode's real benefit is reduced eye fatigue in dim environments
distinct_myths.why_fake: Fabricated and inverted; the actual study found no significant fatigue difference, and light mode outperformed dark mode for reading small text at night.

distinct_myths.stat: Vagaro ships cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), Material Design's exact easing curve, verbatim
distinct_myths.why_fake: False; a direct check of Vagaro's live production CSS found no such curve anywhere. Its real curves are entirely different shapes.

distinct_myths.stat: Booksy ships a close-cousin curve, cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.23,1)
distinct_myths.why_fake: Wrong digit; Booksy's live CSS actually ships the exact Material curve, cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), twice. The 'exact match' belongs to Booksy, not Vagaro.

distinct_myths.stat: Vagaro uses a five-step duration ladder: 0.2s / 0.25s / 0.3s / 0.4s / 1s
distinct_myths.why_fake: Doesn't match live CSS; the dominant explicit duration found sitewide is .35s, with no clean five-step ladder present.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha's motion-duration ladder has six rungs: 100/200/300/500/600/1000ms
distinct_myths.why_fake: Undercounts; the live design tokens actually show a nine-rung ladder (100 through 1200ms), omitting three of the steps.

distinct_myths.stat: Google's RAIL model sets a ~1000ms Load/Idle ceiling that nests inside Nielsen's 1-second rule
distinct_myths.why_fake: Fabricated; RAIL's real published numbers top out at 5 seconds for load-interactive on 3G, none of them near 1000ms.

distinct_myths.stat: None of the four booking competitors uses a spring or overshoot easing curve
distinct_myths.why_fake: Doesn't fully hold; Vagaro's own live CSS contains a classic bouncy overshoot curve.

distinct_myths.stat: Cookie-consent banners use a z-index near Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstates the magnitude by about 4.2 million times; live-measured values all sit near the 32-bit signed-integer ceiling (2,147,483,647), not JavaScript's actual max safe integer.

distinct_myths.stat: Fresha's dialog shadow blur is roughly 2.5x the card shadow's blur
distinct_myths.why_fake: Understates the ratio; live-measured values give roughly 3.3x when comparing the widest blur layer of each.

distinct_myths.stat: rajeshrnair.com's 2026 UI trends roundup recommends a two-layer shadow recipe
distinct_myths.why_fake: Unsourced; the domain is an unrelated IT consultant's personal portfolio site with no matching content, and no search surfaces such an article there.

distinct_myths.stat: zignuts.com flags neumorphism as an accessibility failure
distinct_myths.why_fake: Unsourced; the domain is a corporate dev-agency site with no neumorphism or accessibility content, and it isn't locatable via search either.

distinct_myths.stat: Booksy.com uses zero saturated computed colors anywhere on the page
distinct_myths.why_fake: False; a live scan found a distinctly saturated teal-blue color used 368 times sitewide, including on a visible app-download CTA.

distinct_myths.stat: Booking.com's primary CTA and header both use saturated blue at scale
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstates the CTA half; the header band is genuinely blue, but the actual homepage Search CTA button renders orange/gold, not blue.

distinct_myths.stat: Zocdoc's homepage uses a warm cream/ivory background
distinct_myths.why_fake: False as measured; the live background is a cool light gray, in the same family as Solen's own tokens, not a warm tone.

distinct_myths.stat: Radix Colors documentation states 'practical usability over theoretical uniformity'
distinct_myths.why_fake: This exact quote does not appear anywhere in Radix's actual docs; a fabricated verbatim quote attached to a real, differently-worded idea.

distinct_myths.stat: German UI copy runs about 30% longer than English, per gleef.eu
distinct_myths.why_fake: Traces to a content-farm page attributed to a fake-sounding byline that doesn't actually contain this figure anywhere.

distinct_myths.stat: Treatwell's primary CTA reads the shortened phrase 'Buche 24/7'
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstated; that phrase is a feature-section subheading on the live page, not the button text on Treatwell's actual primary CTA.

distinct_myths.stat: Discord's language-settings rows dynamically wrap to a second line for longer language names
distinct_myths.why_fake: Overstates the behavior; every row is a static two-line design used uniformly regardless of name length, not a dynamic wrap-on-overflow.

distinct_myths.stat: Only 7 specific hooks are wired in settings.json
distinct_myths.why_fake: Undercounts; settings.json actually wires roughly 24 unique hook commands, including two other Stop-hooks the list omits entirely.

owner_decisions.topic: Imagery-density bands for pages (hero, browse, transactional)
owner_decisions.tension: The proposed bands (roughly 35-45% hero imagery, about a third of the page on browse pages, near 0% on transactional pages) are only observed from real apps, not causally tested, so writing them into canon now would lock a CONV-tier guess as if it were proven.
owner_decisions.options: Lock the bands now as directional guidance; hold and test through the Taste Lab first; or keep only the qualitative ordering (hero > browse > transactional) without specific percentages.

owner_decisions.topic: Split map+list view vs list-only for salon search results
owner_decisions.tension: Baymard's research places list-only search results in the underperforming majority of sites, which is where Solen's current salon-search page sits, but adding a split view is a real structural change, not a small tweak.
owner_decisions.options: Add a split map+list view to match the better-performing pattern; keep list-only and accept the tradeoff; or prototype and test split-view before committing.

owner_decisions.topic: Hero-section height percentage for new pages
owner_decisions.tension: Even after correcting the original invented number, competitor hero heights measured this pass (Fresha 40-50%, Treatwell 30-40%) run noticeably higher than the previously-cited 25-30% band, and none of it was pixel-measured by either pass.
owner_decisions.options: Widen Solen's target hero-height band to match the corrected higher range; keep the lower band as a deliberate restraint choice; or get an actual pixel-measured teardown before locking any number.

owner_decisions.topic: Zero-results / no-matching-filters CTA style
owner_decisions.tension: Real competitor precedent for this control is genuinely mixed, not a single dominant pattern as first assumed.
owner_decisions.options: Neutral-outline pill (like Skyscanner); plain text link with no button (like GitHub); solid ink/brand-color fill (like Too Good To Go); or no CTA at all, just a message (like Walmart).

owner_decisions.topic: Responsive grid-column ladder test design (map-open vs map-closed)
owner_decisions.tension: The planned test treats Solen's locked 2/3/4-column grid as one undifferentiated case against Fresha/Airbnb, but the locked rule already branches for map-open state and may already match competitors there; the real open question is only the untested map-closed state.
owner_decisions.options: Split the test into map-open/map-closed cases and focus only on the untested closed state; test both as one case as originally planned; or leave the ladder unchanged until the map-closed state is actually observed on competitors.

owner_decisions.topic: Whether to lock the unverified Uber Base motion-timing number
owner_decisions.tension: The Uber Base 100ms-crossfade / diagonal-movement detail has never actually been directly observed (the site couldn't be scraped) and remains the lowest confidence tier, but it's tempting to harden it into a locked Solen motion token anyway.
owner_decisions.options: Do not lock it until someone directly screenshots or records Uber Base; lock it anyway as a placeholder pending verification; or drop the citation and base the rule only on sources that are verified.

owner_decisions.topic: New-token owner sign-off gate (reaffirmed, not new)
owner_decisions.tension: Any genuinely new semantic color, spacing relationship, or radius role is supposed to require an explicit owner yes logged in TASTE_LOG before it's added, and this stream confirms that gate should keep being enforced.
owner_decisions.options: Keep enforcing the sign-off gate as-is; or relax it for small, low-risk token additions.

owner_decisions.topic: Adopt the house-original visual-balance formula as Solen's canon
owner_decisions.tension: The proposed centroid-based balance-check formula was found to be a Solen-original synthesis, not actually derived from the academic paper it was said to be grounded in.
owner_decisions.options: Adopt the house formula anyway, clearly labeled as house-original rather than academically derived; find or build a formula that genuinely is validated by real research; or drop the computable-balance idea and rely on human judgment instead.

owner_decisions.topic: Blue-accent usage ceiling (tighten or keep)
owner_decisions.tension: Solen's current cap (3 blue elements on content, 1 on a form) was partly supported by external app examples, two of which turned out to be hallucinated Mobbin screens, leaving a smaller and more honest evidence sample than originally presented.
owner_decisions.options: Tighten the ceiling further given the weaker remaining evidence; keep the current ceiling since it was already a deliberate restraint choice; or gather fresh, verified competitor evidence before changing anything.

owner_decisions.topic: Refine the alignment/off-grid detector's numeric tolerance
owner_decisions.tension: The current detector check (value % 5 !== 0 above 100px) is only a loose proxy for the actual LOCKFILE instruction to 'round to clean 5s/10s', and can pass or fail values it shouldn't.
owner_decisions.options: Rewrite the detector to match the LOCKFILE rule more precisely; keep the current loose proxy since it's directionally close; or loosen the LOCKFILE wording to match what's actually checkable.

owner_decisions.topic: Build a fourth mandatory Stop-hook gate (pre-delivery self-walk)
owner_decisions.tension: Three Stop-hooks already block turn-end today; adding a fourth risks gate fatigue or slowing down every single turn, even though the proposed gate covers real ground the others don't.
owner_decisions.options: Build it as a fourth mandatory gate; fold its checks into one of the three existing gates instead; or keep it as advisory-only guidance, not enforced.

owner_decisions.topic: Invest in building 'Taste Lab' tooling
owner_decisions.tension: The repertory-grid / staircase-probe infrastructure this stream describes only elicits and records taste data, it doesn't resolve any open taste question by itself, and there's no build-time estimate yet.
owner_decisions.options: Greenlight building it as real tooling; run the same probes manually/ad hoc without dedicated tooling; or shelve the idea until a concrete taste question actually needs it.

owner_decisions.topic: Canonicalize icon stroke-width
owner_decisions.tension: Icon stroke-width is still a soft/CONV recommendation, not a hard lock, because no single number has been picked yet.
owner_decisions.options: Pick a specific stroke-width value (e.g. match Lucide's default) and lock it; or leave it soft/flexible per icon size.

owner_decisions.topic: Solen's own spacing ladder falls below the proposed 1.25x ratio floor
owner_decisions.tension: Solen's existing reference spacing ladder (16/48/56/72/84) has two steps (48-to-56 and 72-to-84, both 1.17x) that don't clear the newly-proposed 1.25x minimum spacing-ratio floor, and that floor's own sourcing turned out weaker than claimed.
owner_decisions.options: Adjust those two steps in the ladder to hit at least 1.25x; keep the existing ladder and treat 1.25x as advisory-only, not a hard rule; or drop the 1.25x floor since it wasn't well-sourced anyway.

owner_decisions.topic: Split the overflow-audit detector into container-breach vs text-clip flags
owner_decisions.tension: This round found Booking.com's overflow failure is actually a box-position breach (element pushes outside its container), not a self-contained text clip, and these may need to be tracked as genuinely different bug types.
owner_decisions.options: Keep them as two separate detector flags for more precise fixes; or merge into one generic 'overflow' flag for simplicity.

owner_decisions.topic: Severity/priority tier-count band (3 to 5 tiers)
owner_decisions.tension: Only Jira and ClickUp remain fully canonical evidence for the 3-5 tier band after this pass; GitHub Projects and Miro were downgraded to weak/anecdotal, and Airtable/Asana are template-level, not core-product conventions.
owner_decisions.options: Keep the 3-5 tier band since Jira and ClickUp alone are still solid anchors; narrow to exactly Jira's and ClickUp's own tier counts; or hold off locking until more genuinely canonical examples are found.

owner_decisions.topic: Loosen the locked breadcrumb-depth threshold
owner_decisions.tension: Solen currently shows a breadcrumb once a page is 2+ levels deep, but NN/g's actual convention is looser, no breadcrumb needed until 3+ levels deep.
owner_decisions.options: Keep the current 2+ threshold; move to NN/g's looser 3+ threshold; or keep 2+ but make it lighter-weight for the 2-level case.

owner_decisions.topic: Selected/active filter-chip fill color (gray vs saturated color)
owner_decisions.tension: Solen's locked style uses a calm-gray sunken fill for selected filters and pills, but essentially every sampled competitor (Fresha, Beli, Airwallex, N26 dark mode, OpenSea, and others) uses a saturated color fill or an outline ring instead.
owner_decisions.options: Keep Solen's locked calm-gray fill as a deliberate restraint/brand differentiator; move to a colored fill or outline ring to match near-universal competitor convention; or keep gray for filters but allow color for a specific subset like onboarding pills.

owner_decisions.topic: Confidence level for the unread-notification-dot citation
owner_decisions.tension: A direct recheck this pass could not confirm that Booking.com, Expedia, and Grab specifically use the cited unread-dot convention, even though the general pattern is plausible.
owner_decisions.options: Keep the citation but mark it unconfirmed; drop the specific brand names and keep only the general pattern claim; or do a fresh, verified recheck before using it in any locked doc.

owner_decisions.topic: Build the verification pipeline needed for a 'Verified' trust badge
owner_decisions.tension: No data field or verification process currently exists to back a 'Verified' badge, so showing one today would break the no-fabricated-data rule, and building the real pipeline is a real engineering investment with no immediate customer demand (pre-launch).
owner_decisions.options: Prioritize building the verification pipeline so the badge can ship for real; shelve the badge idea until there's a natural reason to build it; or find a different, already-available trust signal instead.

owner_decisions.topic: Destructive-action button color (red vs ink)
owner_decisions.tension: The six-app list originally cited for red destructive buttons had backing evidence for only one app (Notion); Fresha's own admin panel also uses red for delete actions, but Fresha's client-facing cancel-appointment modal is ink-only, so the evidence doesn't cleanly support either a red-everywhere or ink-everywhere rule.
owner_decisions.options: Make destructive actions red, matching the one confirmed precedent; keep destructive actions ink/black for brand consistency, matching the one confirmed client-facing example; or re-verify the other five apps with real screenshots before deciding.

owner_decisions.topic: Reconcile copy-economy rule with accessibility explainer-copy needs
owner_decisions.tension: Solen's 'drop words the context already says' copy rule conflicts with the accessibility finding that toggle/settings labels genuinely need a full explanatory sentence to be usable with a screen reader.
owner_decisions.options: Carve out an explicit accessibility exception to the copy-economy rule for toggle descriptions; keep labels short visually but add the fuller sentence only in screen-reader-only text; or apply copy-economy everywhere and accept the accessibility tradeoff.

owner_decisions.topic: Add a dark-mode toggle on web
owner_decisions.tension: Solen's locked decision is light-only, no toggle, on web, but NN/g's actual (corrected) recommendation for general-population products is to let users switch to dark mode if they want it.
owner_decisions.options: Keep the light-only-no-toggle decision as a deliberate brand choice; add a user-facing dark-mode toggle to follow NN/g's recommendation; or revisit only once real usage data exists post-launch.

owner_decisions.topic: Re-source the 1-second perceived-load ceiling
owner_decisions.tension: The claimed RAIL corroboration for a ~1-second load ceiling turned out to be fabricated (RAIL has no ~1000ms tier), so the rule now rests on Nielsen/Miller alone instead of the 'three independently-sourced bands' originally claimed.
owner_decisions.options: Keep the 1-second ceiling sourced to Nielsen/Miller only and drop the RAIL claim; find a different second source before treating it as well-corroborated; or do a live recheck of Booking.com's own timing values before citing them anywhere.

owner_decisions.topic: Restructure the z-index ladder into decade-jump tiers
owner_decisions.tension: Solen's current z-index scale (400/410/500/510/600/700) uses closely-spaced numbers, while live measurements of Booking.com, Treatwell, and Booksy all use much more widely-spaced tiers, now more firmly evidenced than before.
owner_decisions.options: Restructure to wider decade-jump tiers now that it's better evidenced; keep the current tighter scale since it hasn't caused real collision bugs; or widen only the closest-spaced layers rather than the whole ladder.

owner_decisions.topic: Fix the blue accent color's contrast failure on sunken backgrounds
owner_decisions.tension: The accent color only reaches 4.17:1 contrast against the sunken gray background, confirmed below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for text, tracing to its current lightness value.
owner_decisions.options: Adjust the accent's lightness until it clears 4.5:1 on sunken backgrounds; keep the current color and restrict its use on sunken backgrounds specifically; or accept the gap since most sunken-background uses are non-text/decorative.

owner_decisions.topic: Approve a companion edit to SOURCE.md for i18n text-expansion findings
owner_decisions.tension: SOURCE.md outranks RATIONALE.md in the doc hierarchy, so a proposed edit there needs explicit owner sign-off and cannot be auto-applied, even though the underlying finding is solid.
owner_decisions.options: Approve the SOURCE.md edit as proposed; or decline and keep the finding in RATIONALE.md only.

owner_decisions.topic: Bucket copy strings in the 51-70 character range for i18n
owner_decisions.tension: Strings in the 51-70 character range don't cleanly fit any existing i18n text-expansion length bucket.
owner_decisions.options: Create a new dedicated bucket for 51-70 char strings; or fold them into an adjacent existing bucket.
